0.0.n: A regional name forming the first part of the company name 伊予鉄道.

0.1.n: Together with 伊予, this forms the company name Iyo Railway.

0.2.n: Marks Iyo Railway as the network where the following situation applies.

0.3.n: Makes the railway network the topic, attaching to で.

0.4.n: This is a castle name; 城 means castle.

0.5.n: Marks Matsuyama Castle as what the routes encircle with 囲む.

0.6.n: Adds the image of going in a complete circle.

0.7.n: Links ぐるり to 囲む, describing how the routes surround the castle.

0.8.n: The plain form describes the routes' arrangement before ように.

0.9.n: Follows 囲む and combines with に to describe how the routes are arranged.

0.10.n: Completes ように, making the preceding description explain the routes' layout.

1.0.n: Combines with 電車 to refer to the city's tram service.

1.1.n: Although often meaning trains, 電車 refers to street-running trams here.

1.2.n: Connects the city tram service to its routes.

1.3.n: Refers to the tram lines, rather than individual vehicles.

1.4.n: Marks 路線 as the thing whose existence and number are stated.

1.5.n: Uses the general counting form ending in つ to count the routes.

1.6.n: The plain form of the verb used for the existence of things, rather than people or animals.

1.7.n: Short for の, adding an explanatory tone before だ.

1.8.n: Completes the casual explanatory ending んだ; it is not a separate is here.

1.9.n: Adds a friendly sense of telling the listener something they may not know.

2.0.n: Before の and a noun, this refers to the great majority of that group.

2.1.n: Connects ほとんど to 路線, identifying the group being described.

2.2.n: Refers back to the city tram lines introduced earlier.

2.3.n: Marks most routes as the subject of 運行しています.

2.4.n: Gives the lower end of the range of time between services.

2.5.n: Introduces the starting value of the ten-to-fifteen-minute range.

2.6.n: Includes の, which links the full time range to 間隔.

2.7.n: Refers to the time gaps between successive tram services.

2.8.n: Marks the intervals at which the trams operate.

2.9.n: 運行する becomes 運行しています, a polite form describing regular ongoing service rather than just this moment.

0.lit: On Iyo Railway, as for, in a way that encircles Matsuyama Castle all the way around…
0.tip: 囲むように describes the routes' layout here, rather than expressing a purpose.

1.lit: City tram routes, five exist, you see.
1.tip: あるんだよ combines a statement of existence with a casual, friendly explanatory ending.

2.lit: Most of the routes operate at intervals of ten to fifteen minutes.
2.tip: The の after 15分 links the entire range, 10分から15分, to 間隔.
